sweep5.detail: Walked the spec's sections in order and proved each named artefact where the spec puts it. Actors -> Organization.nextRequestNumber (schema.prisma:169, migration.sql:11). Roles matrix -> 6 capabilities, lowercase-dashed in CAPABILITY_MATRIX (index.ts:582-712) and PascalCase in roles.ts, grants matching the matrix row for row. Functional requirements 1-47 -> validators and parsers in packages/validation/src/requests.ts, service methods in requests.service.ts, 11 routes in requests.controller.ts. Data Model -> 3 tables, 21+6+11 columns, 6 indexes incl. the unique (organizationId, number), 9 FKs with the stated onDelete. New Enums -> a deliberate 'none', and none exist. Error Messages -> 31 REQUEST_MESSAGES keys, text matching the table word for word, extended in place with no duplicate key. Required data-testid -> all 42 present under apps/web (4 via template literal, checked by hand) and referenced from e2e. Test Cases -> all 41 ids (6 UNIT, 22 INT, 13 E2E) referenced in code. 'What this spec does not send' (requirement 47) -> negative artefact confirmed: no file under apps/api/src/mail is in the diff and the requests module imports no mail service. No section contributed zero artefacts except Out of Scope and Known Gaps, which state non-goals.

findings.claim: The prompt strings this diff adds carry history and justification rather than rules. Lines 131-132 emit a heading naming a prior run id and the sentence 'These blockers are older than the working tree and were raised before the spec was corrected'; line 174 emits 'never from what an agent appeared to open, which cannot be told from a journal of tool calls', which is why the rule exists. Every pre_implement, implement and review invocation pays for those sentences. The rule form is already present beside them at :133-135 ('Verify each against the current code first ... Do not take any of them as a current fact'), so nothing is lost by deleting the prose.

witness.detail: CLAUDE.md:158-166 — '**Agent prompts are rules only.** ... Never put in a prompt: measurements, counts, timings or costs from this project; what happened on an earlier run, or what some agent did last time; why a rule exists, what it replaced, or a link to the reasoning. Write the conclusion, not the evidence for it. ... Every sentence of justification is paid for on every invocation and changes no behaviour.' The offending strings are added by this diff: `git diff f06c7d8...HEAD -- scripts/ship.mjs` shows :131-132 and :174 as `+` lines. The findings payload itself is not at issue — it is the workflow's documented mechanism; the history and reasoning wrapped around it are.

findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the carried heading to '## Carried findings' plus the existing verify-first rule at :133-135, dropping the run id, 'older than the working tree' and 'before the spec was corrected'. At :174 keep 'It is derived from the commit each earlier verdict names as judged and the files it reported unreached' and delete the clause after the dash. dismissedShardClaims.claim: TC-01-INT-13's route 1 is a tautology because Honolulu and Kiritimati share a calendar date for roughly 14 of every 24 hours.
dismissedShardClaims.whyDismissed: The arithmetic is wrong. Honolulu is UTC-10 and Kiritimati UTC+14, exactly 24 hours apart, so the eastern local date is the western date plus one at every instant and `westToday < eastToday` is always true — the assertion at apps/api/test/requests.spec.ts:753 always demands overdue: true. Both dates are computed in the test with Intl directly, not through the code under test, so an isRequestOverdue that always returned false would fail it. The case is deterministic and guards what the spec's corrected TC-01-INT-13 asks for.
